resources.string:
The magic keyboard is a built-in input method that lets you pick credentials without leaving the current app.

When a text field is focused, a persistent notification lets you open the keyboard, search your database and insert the username, password or other field directly.

It never connects to the network and never reads what you type; it only fills the value you explicitly choose.

Copy actions place the value on the system clipboard temporarily.

For security the clipboard is cleared automatically after the configured timeout, and sensitive values are never logged.

On Android 12 and later the system may show a preview or allow other apps to read the clipboard; prefer in-place autofill when it is available.

PmVault can act as the system Autofill service (Android 8+).

When you tap a login field, Android shows matching entries above the keyboard; selecting one fills the form. On a save or password-change screen PmVault can offer to save the new entry or update the password of an existing one, similar to a browser password manager.

Enable it in system settings and keep the database unlocked for filling; saving does not require unlocking.

Passkeys replace passwords with a key pair stored in your database.

The private key never leaves the device; only a public key is registered with the website, so phishing and leaked-server passwords no longer apply.

Passkey support requires a recent Android version and a website/app that explicitly supports passkeys (WebAuthn / FIDO2).
